entities.name: Willem Schouten
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Willem Cornelisz Schouten (died 1625) was a Dutch navigator and explorer whose 1615–1617 expedition, undertaken with Jacob Le Maire, irrevocably altered the landscape of global maritime trade and cartography by successfully circumnavigating the southern tip of South America. This voyage, which charted the perilous passage around Cape Horn, definitively proved that Tierra del Fuego was an island, not part of a vast southern continent, and established a crucial, albeit dangerous, new route between the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans, thereby challenging the monopolistic control of the Dutch East India Company.

Departing from Hoorn, Netherlands, on June 14, 1615, Schouten commanded the *Eendracht* while Le Maire led the *Hoorn*. Their primary objective, sponsored by the Australian Company, was to find a new passage into the Pacific that bypassed the Strait of Magellan, which was exclusively controlled by the Dutch East India Company (VOC) under their charter. On January 29, 1616, Schouten and Le Maire successfully rounded a foreboding landmass, naming the newly discovered cape 'Kaap Hoorn' after Schouten's hometown. This achievement was preceded by the tragic loss of the *Hoorn* to fire, leaving the *Eendracht* to complete the journey, navigating the Pacific and eventually reaching Batavia (modern Jakarta) in October 1616.
